judgements.skipSteelman: Zero evidence in 266 commits (the ENTIRE repo history, 2026-07-11 to 2026-09-17 — the whole repo fits inside the 3-month window). Three independent proxies all came back empty (see partialCommitEvidence). The workflow this guard assumes — `git add -p`, or staging then re-editing — is a multi-developer / code-review habit; this repo is one developer plus agents committing whole milestones, median 4 files, up to 51. Worse for the guard: `git commit -a` stages tracked modifications BEFORE the pre-commit hook runs, so `git diff --name-only` is already empty and the guard is a silent no-op for that entire workflow. The proposal as written is also placed at line 21, ABOVE the docs-only fast-path exit at line 26 — so it would refuse on the 87/266 (33%) of commits where the gate does not run build/test/lint at all. On a third of commits it is pure friction protecting nothing, by construction. And the failure it prevents (a broken HEAD) is one this repo has never demonstrably had: all 6 red CI runs are explained by a different cause.
judgements.bittenUsEvidence: NONE FOUND. Proxy 1 (adjacent-commit overlap on non-.md files, newer commit <=2 files and <=12 lines): 0 hits across 265 adjacent pairs. Loosened to <=5 files / <=60 lines: 3 hits, all three read and all three deliberate — 2d646df is a milestone explicitly labelled 'Stage 2 M9 (partial)' (5 files: RESUME_HERE + SESSION-LOG + 2 src + a baseline json), c46adbc is 'Pin the stack in dependabot' (dependabot.yml + package-lock.json, the lockfile is the point), b4e361b is a named adversarial-pass correction to tests/npcSlice3a.plants.ts. Proxy 2 (commit-subject scan for forgot|unstaged|partial|missed|amend|oops|hotfix|broke|revert): 40 hits, every one of them the literal words 'Stage N' or a deliberate '(partial)' scope label — zero staging accidents. Proxy 3 (docs/sessions/-SESSION-LOG.md, 3971 lines, grep for no-verify|unstaged|forgot to stage|partial commit|index vs|working tree): 2 hits, both unrelated prose ('Staged the live-CDN client SWFs', 'staged, both facing one way'). Proxy 4, the one that would have been the smoking gun: 6 push-to-master CI runs are RED and ALL SIX failed at exactly `npm test`, the step the local gate also runs — the precise signature of 'gate green locally, red on what actually landed'. I read the logs: every one is `ENOENT` on `reference/decompiled/...` and `reference/extracted/...`, the gitignored study corpus CI can never have. Not one is a partial commit.

standingCost.secondsPerCommit: +0.012 s, MEASURED (`time git diff --name-only` = 0.012 s; `git diff --cached --name-only` = 0.006 s) against a ~8 s gate. Seconds are NOT the cost of this candidate and I will not pretend they are — the entire cost is false reds and the --no-verify habit they train.
standingCost.falseRedFrequency: Structurally low in the narrow (intersection) form — it fires only when the SAME path is both staged and further modified. Not measurable from history (staging state leaves no trace), so I cannot put a number on it and will not invent one. What IS measured: as proposed (inserted at line 21, above the fast-path exit at line 26) it is live on the 87/266 = 33% of commits that are markdown-only, where the gate runs nothing and there is nothing to protect. Moving it below line 26 removes that whole class for free.
standingCost.linesToMaintain: 4-6 lines of POSIX sh inside the one file that can block every commit in the repo.
standingCost.newFailureModes: MEASURED, and it is worse than the brief's caveat: `<(...)` is not merely 'needs bash' — under this machine's `/bin/sh` (bash 3.2.57 in POSIX mode) `cat <(echo x)` is a hard **syntax error** ('syntax error near unexpected token `('). The proposed one-liner would break the hook outright, not degrade. Second: the hook inherits PATH `grep`, and this user's interactive shell shims `grep` to `ugrep` — I checked, and under `sh` it resolves to `/usr/bin/grep` (BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD), so the shim does NOT reach the hook; that worry is refuted. Third: I tested `grep -Fxf` with an empty pattern file and it matched nothing, so an empty STAGED is safe. Fourth, the real one: a refusal in a hook during a long autonomous agent session blocks a milestone commit at a moment when no human is watching the terminal, and the documented recovery in this account is the salvage pattern ('commit at every checkpoint') — a guard that can stop a checkpoint commit is in direct tension with the mitigation that has already saved 3 workflow deaths.

judgements.simplerVersion:
WARN, do not refuse, and put it BELOW the docs-only fast path (after line 26, not after line 21). POSIX-safe, no process substitution: `git diff --name-only > /tmp/gate-wt.$$; PARTIAL=$(printf '%s
' "$STAGED" | grep -Fxf /tmp/gate-wt.$$); rm -f /tmp/gate-wt.$$; [ -n "$PARTIAL" ] && printf '
[gate] NOTE: staged files also have unstaged edits — the gate below tests the WORKING TREE, not what you are committing:
%s

' "$PARTIAL"`. ~5 lines, 12 ms, cannot block anything, and prints a line whose diagnostic value is highest exactly where it is needed (an agent committing a milestone unattended). This is JClaw's own resolution for the identical judgement call: /tmp/jclaw/.githooks/pre-commit:64-66 — 'Informational only ... a hard block would just train you to reach for --no-verify.'
judgements.why: This is the weakest BUILD I would sign, and DROP is defensible: 0/266 evidence, and a WARN nobody ever sees is 5 dead lines of ceremony. It earns the nod only because the warn form is 5 lines and 12 ms, cannot train --no-verify, and JClaw already settled this exact trade the same way (:64-66). BUILD-SIMPLER is conditional on all three corrections: (1) WARN not refuse, (2) below the fast path at line 26 so the 33% markdown-only commits never see it, (3) no process substitution — measured to be a syntax error under this repo's `/bin/sh`. The proposal as written fails (1), (2) and (3). Note also the scope honesty the brief itself gives: JClaw does not have our problem — its hook is `#!/usr/bin/env bash` running lint-staged on staged files only, and it deliberately keeps the full suites in PRE-PUSH ('this hook must stay fast (< 5 s typical) so rapid commits aren't disrupted', :2-4). We run the whole suite in pre-commit, which is what creates the staged-vs-tree gap in the first place.

judgements.skipSteelman: Same defect, same repo, worse scope — this is a duplicate of gate-guards-6 and the cluster should dedupe to one. Its proposal is the BROAD refusal: 'if any tracked file differs between the index and the working tree, fail with the list.' That is not the partial-commit condition; it is the 'you have any uncommitted work at all' condition, and it refuses commits that are in no way partial. Its premise — 'in this single-developer repo a partial commit is always accidental' — is the sentence that breaks it: in this repo a divergence between index and working tree is usually DELIBERATE, because the documented workflow commits a doc (RESUME_HERE.md is 'rewritten ... in the SAME commit as the change it describes') and stages milestone slices while an agent keeps editing source. The JClaw evidence also does not support the broad form: JClaw applies `git show :` to exactly ONE guard (the pnpm lockfile pin, :33-37), and the brief's own 'scope honesty' line concedes it — lint-staged handles the general case and the full suite runs pre-push on the checked-out tree. Nobody, including JClaw, built what this candidate proposes.
judgements.bittenUsEvidence: NONE FOUND — identical to gate-guards-6 above; it is the same defect. Nothing in 266 commits, 3971 log lines, or 13 push-to-master CI runs shows a partial commit.

standingCost.secondsPerCommit: +0.012 s measured — again, not the cost.
standingCost.falseRedFrequency: MEASURED LOWER BOUND: 15 of 266 commits (5.6%) are a markdown-only commit followed by a code commit within 30 minutes, with gaps of 41 s, 112 s, 168 s, 270 s, 274 s, 369 s, 461 s, 462 s, 621 s. At a 41-second gap the source edits were already sitting in the working tree when the docs commit was made — the broad guard would have REFUSED those 15 commits outright. That is a floor, not an estimate: it misses every case where the in-flight code was committed later than 30 minutes or abandoned, and it misses all 154 mixed md+code commits where a staged slice was committed while other files stayed dirty. A guard firing on at least 1 commit in 18 of normal workflow is a guard that gets bypassed, and CLAUDE.md line 49 already advertises the bypass on every single run ('bypass with --no-verify'). Once --no-verify is the reflex, typecheck, tests and lint stop running too — the guard would cost more safety than it buys. LIVE FALSE RED, OBSERVED RIGHT NOW, NOT A PROXY: at the close of this run `git status --porcelain` shows three tracked files modified-and-unstaged (docs/research/runs/jclaw-2026-09-14/study-agent-instructions.json, study-harness-evolution.json, study-hooks-ci-sandbox.json) while the deliverable this cluster produces sits untracked in refute/. The broad guard would REFUSE the very commit that lands this run's output. That is the guard firing on the workflow that is building it.
standingCost.linesToMaintain: ~6 lines, plus the standing cost of an override reflex that disables the other three checks.
standingCost.newFailureModes: Trains `--no-verify` on a hook that is this repo's ONLY working quality gate (CI is red, see notJudged). It also inverts the salvage rule: it can refuse a checkpoint commit mid-autonomous-run, which is exactly what 'commit at every checkpoint' exists to prevent. And it is a no-op under `git commit -a` (git updates the index before the hook runs), so the workflows most likely to be careless are the ones it never inspects.

judgements.simplerVersion: Do not build it separately. It collapses into gate-guards-6's warn line with zero loss — the narrow intersection catches the real defect (staged-then-edited) and the broad form adds only false reds. If the cluster wants one line in the hook, it is the gate-guards-6 warn.
judgements.why: Duplicate defect with a strictly worse rule, and the only candidate here with a MEASURED false-red floor of 5.6% of commits against zero measured defects. The failure mode the brief warned about — 'a guard that fires on normal workflow gets bypassed with --no-verify, and then it protects nothing' — is not hypothetical for this one; it is arithmetic. Simplest change wins, and the simplest change is the one line in gate-guards-6, not this.

partialCommitEvidence.method: Four proxies over the FULL history (266 commits, 2026-07-11 first commit to 2026-09-17 — the entire repo is inside the ~3-month window, so this is a census, not a sample). (1) Adjacent-pair overlap: for each of the 265 adjacent commit pairs, the intersection of non-.md paths touched by both, keeping pairs where the newer commit is small; run at two thresholds. (2) `git log --format=%s` scanned for forgot|unstaged|partial|missed|amend|stage|hotfix|broke|broken|revert|oops|typo. (3) docs/sessions/-SESSION-LOG.md (3971 lines) scanned for no-verify|unstaged|forgot to stage|partial commit|index vs|working tree. (4) `gh run list` + `gh run view --log-failed` over all GitHub Actions runs, isolating push-to-master, then reading the failure cause of every red run — because a partial commit's signature is 'local gate green, CI test step red on the same code'.
partialCommitEvidence.note: Stated plainly: partial staging leaves NO trace in git history, so 'suspectedPartials: 0' means 'no evidence of', never 'proven never happened'. The specific blind spot: a partial commit whose committed tree still typechecks and passes tests (e.g. an unstaged comment, a doc tweak, a half-finished edit in a file the tests do not reach) is invisible to all four proxies — and in a repo where 33% of commits are markdown-only and the gate skips them anyway, that is plausibly the common case. What the proxies DO establish is that no partial commit has ever produced a visible consequence: no follow-up fix-up commit, no staging language in 266 subjects or 3971 log lines, and none of the 6 red CI runs. Strongest single datum: all 6 red push-to-master runs failed at `npm test` — the exact signature we were hunting — and all 6 turned out to be `reference/` ENOENT, which refutes rather than supports the defect.

notJudged: HIGHER-VALUE FINDING, OUT OF SCOPE FOR C5 BUT IT INVERTS THE 'DO NOTHING, CI CATCHES IT' OPTION. The brief's fallback — '.github/workflows/ci.yml runs lint/test/build on every push to master, so a broken partial commit is caught at push time' — is FALSE TODAY, measured. Every push-to-master CI run since 2026-08-24 has been RED: 6 consecutive failures (45114a0 09-14, 995bb52 09-08, 40685f8 09-07, 8f9f4d4 08-25, 6176713 08-24, 91c6010 08-24). Last green push: 962a005, 2026-08-24 — 24 days of red. All 6 fail at `npm test` with 6 failed suites (tests/ogActorConsts, ogAiData, ogCompositing, ogItemData, ogNpcData, ogSkillData) throwing ENOENT on reference/decompiled/*.as and reference/extracted/*.xml. `reference/` is gitignored BY INVARIANT (study-only, never distributed), so CI structurally cannot ever pass those suites. This is textbook fail-open accounting from this account's own memory: a real regression pushed today would be the 7th consecutive red and indistinguishable from the standing noise. Two more measured facts that finish the point: only 13 push-to-master runs exist for 266 commits (CI sees a batched tip, never each commit, so a broken intermediate commit is invisible to it by design), and master is RIGHT NOW 3 commits ahead of origin/master, so CI has not seen the 3 most recent commits at all. Recommendation: this is worth more than either C5 candidate combined — make those 6 suites skip-with-a-loud-SKIPPED when reference/ is absent, the way CLAUDE.md says claimcheck already does ('without it the run says loudly that it checked NOTHING'), so CI goes green and a red run means something again.

I did not verify the ~8 s gate figure from the context — running the full vitest suite on this 8 GB machine is expensive and non-essential, since the added guard measures 12 ms either way and the argument never turns on gate duration.

I could not test whether any historical commit's tree actually fails typecheck/test — that needs `git checkout`/worktree, which the contract forbids in this repo. The CI log read is the substitute and it is the better evidence anyway.
